facts.title: A finger points across a counting house
facts.body: Caravaggio’s Calling of Saint Matthew (c. 1600) drops the Gospel into a dim Roman tavern of tax collectors — grace arriving as a shaft of light.

facts.title: Christ almost at the door
facts.body: Christ stands at the right edge, hand echoing Michelangelo’s Adam in reverse — a summoning gesture rather than a gift of life.

facts.title: Peter as escort
facts.body: Peter leans in beside Christ, repeating the pointing hand — the Church guiding the call.

facts.title: Who, me?
facts.body: Matthew (or the bearded man at the table, depending on reading) reacts to the light — surprise caught mid-count.

facts.title: Light as theology
facts.body: A hard diagonal beam cuts the darkness — Caravaggio’s tenebrism making revelation physical.

facts.title: Money on the table
facts.body: Coins and ledgers mark Matthew’s old life as a tax collector — the world he is asked to leave.

facts.title: A shuttered square
facts.body: The window above is closed; light does not come from glass but from an unseen divine source.

facts.title: Velvet and swords
facts.body: Young men in fashionable dress lean over the table — contemporary Rome dressed into scripture.
